name: Brain Network Cooperation
summary: How distributed neural networks collaborate to produce complex mental processes.

sections.heading: Major Brain Networks
sections.content: The Central Executive Network handles focused attention and working memory (PFC and parietal). The Default Mode Network manages self-reflection, imagination, and social cognition. The Salience Network detects important stimuli and switches between other networks. The Sensorimotor Network coordinates perception with action. The Visual Network processes and interprets visual information.

sections.heading: Dynamic Connectivity
sections.content: The brain constantly reconfigures which networks are active and how they interact. The salience network acts as a 'switch operator,' toggling between the externally-focused executive network and the internally-focused default mode network. Dysfunction in this switching mechanism is implicated in ADHD and depression.

sections.heading: Emergent Consciousness
sections.content: Consciousness itself may arise from the global integration of information across distributed brain networks — the Global Workspace Theory proposes that conscious awareness occurs when information is 'broadcast' widely across the cortex, making it available to multiple cognitive processes simultaneously.
